steps.text: Mix together cider vinegar, salt, cayenne pepper, red pepper flakes, light brown sugar, and hot pepper sauce in a large bowl. Stir until salt and brown sugar have dissolved.
Cover and let stand at least 3 hours before using as a basting sauce or serving on meat.

raw_recipe.headline: Eastern North Carolina Barbeque Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This vinegar-based BBQ sauce recipe is piquant and spicy, and popular in eastern North Carolina. It's great for all barbecue meat, but best on pork.
raw_recipe.name: Eastern North Carolina Barbeque Sauce

review.reviewBody: I made this sauce and let it sit for 24 hrs. Then I submerged a pork tenderloin in it for another 24 hrs in the refrigerator.I baked the pork with a small amount of sauce poured over it for 3 hrs at 325 degrees, covered, basting once an hr. Then I shredded the meat with 2 forks and poured the rest of the sauce over it, turned off the oven and when it was time to eat (about 1 1/2 hrs later)popped it on buns and ate heartily. Loved it! Nice & spicy!

Wow! This was perfect! About 3 years ago, I had been to a family reunion in NC where there was a pig roast, and they served the pork with a delicious spicy vinegar dressing that I'd never tried before. Since then, I've had a craving for this sauce. I scaled the sauce by half and made last night. Today, I put a half picnic in my slow cooker all day while I was at work. I added about 1/4 cup of the sauce over the pork while cooking. After draining and shredding the pork, I mixed about 3/4 of the remainder of the sauce with the shredded pork. I served with some homemade cole slaw, homemade corn bread and baked beans and it was just great! Thanks so much. My search for a great Carolina BBQ recipe is over. Thanks so much!!

I'm from New Bern , North Carolina and you simply must cook your pork in this sauce for your pulled pork to taste like what I grew up with. Put your pork and sauce in a slow cooker and let it cook eight hours for a six portion cut of meat, use one to one and a half cups sauce in the cooker with the pork. It will come out juicy and perfect for pulled pork sandwiches , New Bern style of course.

Wow! Delicious. I cooked the heck out of a pork roast in the crockpot with a little chicken broth, then shredded it and soaked it in this sauce. I halved the recipe because it really makes a lot. Served it with cole slaw on top on a kaiser roll. Don't know if this is the proper southern way to enjoy it (I'm from New Jersey), but man was it good. Have made it several times now and it always turns out perfect. Great to serve at a cookout.

Great sauce with spicy and flavour. The acid in the vinegar is for cutting thru fat in meat. So funny to see people saying "too vinegary" when the recipe is pure vinegar plus spices. Add more brown sugar - taste it before serving. All about balance with the food
Halved the recipe, subbed dark brown sugar, and used more red chili flakes since I was out of hot sauce. So easy, and so darn good.

I made it adjusted down for nine serv. from looking at other recipes, I omitted the cayenne cuz pepper flakes made it hot enough, I added 1/2 tsp Worcestershire sauce and 1/2 tap granulated onion powder. Great

I’ve made this a few times and my family loves it!! The first time I made it, I followed the recipe verbatim. The next time, instead of using red pepper flakes, I substituted 1 Tablespoon of Cayenne powder.

My question is this... should the 1 cup of light brown sugar be full-on packed or just lightly packed? If I remember correctly, I think the lightly packed wasn’t quite sweet enough. I wonder if “Lori” the recipe owner can clarify for me.

All I can say is oh my goodness! This is so good! I grew up in southeastern NC, and I grew up on this type of BBQ. It's just like I remember at family dinners growing up. My husband who is from Iowa said this BBQ recipe was better than some of the restaurants in NC who serve this. I accidently put a little more hot sauce than called for, so I ended up putting a tad bit more brown sugar in it to even out the taste. I wanted to make sure my son could eat it also. I slow cooked a pork tenderloin in the oven for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, shredded the meat with two forks, and then poured the sauce over it. I drained all of the excess sauce back into a cup just in case my husband wanted a little extra, but we ended up not needing it. Thank you so much for posting this recipe! Now when I move to Iowa in 6 months, I can bring a piece of home with me! :)

Okay yesterday. Great today! I have given up any notion of finding N.C. barbecue here in Georgia. Parents from Lenoir Co. so father would always take us to Kings, or they would cater our family reunions. Only using a 4-lb Boston Butt , I did half the recipe, and still had more than enough. Just didn't have any cayenne peppers, so skipped that ingredient (Texas Pete sufficed). Made this with hush puppies, coleslaw, and sweet potatoes for a real taste of home.

My family is from Eastern North Carolina
(Smithfield N.C.), and this recipe is right on time. Sometimes we leave out the brown sugar, and use beer for a different kick. This mop sauce is used for roasting the pig, for chopped BBQ. I use it when grilling chops, ribs or a pork shoulder which I grilled a couple a days ago. Very good, give it a try. (TIP!!!! if you really want that eastern North Carolina taste add a little hickory or oak wood to your coals.
The best ….. true Eastern NC BBQ sauce.
I don't like mine quite so spicy, so I only use 1 TBSP cayenne pepper. I also do not add the hot sauce since it is essentially cayenne pepper and vinegar anyway and both are already present.
This is my go to recipe. I use the adjust button to avoid making quarts of sauce, but adjust button hasn't worked in a while and I'm no good at making the adjustments on my own.
I loved the sauce just the way it was. I did double the recipe.
I recommend not using the cayenne peppers and use ketchup instead to give it a thickness to it. But other than that, it is pretty good and taste like Smithfield Chicken and BBQ's sauce.

Nice and spicy, goes well with Pulled Pork.
This sauce is so good. Best one I've tried.
